incident.location: service yard behind The Lantern Rooms, Harbour Yard, Northport
incident.summary: After a private music event, a short confrontation occurred in a poorly lit service yard. The prosecution theory is that Daniel Mercer struck Idris Bell with a metal torch and that Saira Nadeem then pushed or kicked him while he was unsteady or on the ground. CCTV is incomplete and does not clearly show the decisive head impact. Idris Bell walked with assistance, later deteriorated, was admitted to hospital and died on 16 February 2026. Mechanism, individual causal contribution and intent are disputed.
incident.neutralityRule: Allegations and expert hypotheses must not be promoted to findings of fact.

defendants.name: Daniel Mercer
defendants.prosecutionAllegation: Delivered a forceful blow to the left side of Idris Bell's head with a metal torch, intending at least really serious injury.
defendants.defencePosition: Admits holding the torch and a brief confrontation but denies striking the head; says Idris fell after stepping backwards on a kerb.

defendants.name: Saira Nadeem
defendants.prosecutionAllegation: Intentionally pushed or kicked Idris Bell during the confrontation and thereby made a legally significant contribution to the fatal injury or dangerous sequence.
defendants.defencePosition: Admits approaching and pushing an arm away but denies kicking, causing a fall, assisting Daniel Mercer or foreseeing serious violence.

frozenDesignFacts: Idris Bell had a prescribed anticoagulant recorded in primary-care and hospital material.
He had consumed alcohol before the incident.
He was initially responsive and later deteriorated.
Clinical response timing is relevant but no clinician is accused of an offence in this matter.
deceasedMedicalContext.safeRule: Medication, alcohol and clinical care may be contributing/contextual factors; none may be described as an independent or superseding cause without qualified expert support and legal review.

hardSeparationRules: D1 and D2 acts, intent, interviews, admissions and evidence must remain separately scoped.
A proposed charge is not an operative charge or judicial finding.
Pathology mechanism opinion is not proof of actor identity or intent.

No AI-generated conclusion may determine whether treatment, alcohol or anticoagulants break or preserve legal causation; factual contribution, medical cause, susceptibility, alleged intervening act, expert opinion, party submission, court ruling and verdict remain distinct.
Toxicology concentration is not a behavioural or causation conclusion without a stated expert basis.
Admission, agreed fact, prosecution assertion, expert opinion and judicial finding are distinct states.
Death after clinical treatment does not by itself resolve legal causation.
